results.name: odd_set_parity_generalisation
results.description: In multi-example sets whose examples are all odd with at least two distinct final digits, yes-rate on odd targets not matching any example's final digit minus yes-rate on even targets; observed > null means the model under-produces an 'odd numbers' rule (too little parity credit when the shared feature is parity, not digit).
results.code:
# name: odd_set_parity_generalisation
# description: In multi-example sets whose examples are all odd with at least two distinct final digits, yes-rate on odd targets not matching any example's final digit minus yes-rate on even targets; observed > null means the model under-produces an 'odd numbers' rule (too little parity credit when the shared feature is parity, not digit).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, cats = pd.factorize(sets)
    ok = []
    digs = []
    for s in cats:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ds = set(x % 10 for x in xs)
        digs.append(ds)
        ok.append(len(xs) >= 2 and all(x % 2 == 1 for x in xs) and len(ds) >= 2)
    ok = np.array(ok)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    td = t % 10
    match = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for i, ds in enumerate(digs):
        m = codes == i
        match[m] = np.isin(td[m], list(ds))
    inset = ok[codes]
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = inset & (t % 2 == 1) & ~match
    b = inset & (t % 2 == 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: round_target_in_nonround_sets
results.description: In multi-example sets with no example ending in 0, yes-rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes-rate on other even targets not matching any example's final digit; observed != null means the model mis-handles the special status of round numbers (it treats 0 as just another even digit).
results.code:
# name: round_target_in_nonround_sets
# description: In multi-example sets with no example ending in 0, yes-rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes-rate on other even targets not matching any example's final digit; observed != null means the model mis-handles the special status of round numbers (it treats 0 as just another even digit).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, cats = pd.factorize(sets)
    ok = np.array([("," in s) and all(int(x) % 10 != 0 for x in s.split(",")) for s in cats])
    digs = [set(int(x) % 10 for x in s.split(",")) for s in cats]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    td = t % 10
    match = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for i, ds in enumerate(digs):
        m = codes == i
        match[m] = np.isin(td[m], list(ds))
    inset = ok[codes]
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = inset & (td == 0)
    b = inset & (td % 2 == 0) & (td != 0) & ~match
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: singleton_vs_four_example_rate
results.description: Overall yes-rate for one-example sets minus yes-rate for four-example sets; observed > null means the model under-produces the broader generalisation from a single example relative to larger sets (size principle), observed < null the reverse.

results.name: trial_order_drift
results.description: Yes-rate on trials with trial_index above the median minus yes-rate at or below it; a nonzero observed value outside the null (which has no time dependence) means the model misses a drift in willingness to say yes over the session (positive = people get more liberal later).

results.name: singleton_target_magnitude_slope
results.description: For one-example sets, the OLS slope of yes (0/1) on |target - example|/100; observed more negative than null means the model under-produces the decline of acceptance with numeric distance from a lone example.
results.code:
# name: singleton_target_magnitude_slope
# description: For one-example sets, the OLS slope of yes (0/1) on |target - example|/100; observed more negative than null means the model under-produces the decline of acceptance with numeric distance from a lone example.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",").to_numpy()
    if single.sum() < 3:
        return 0.0
    x = s[single].astype(int).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[single]
    d = np.abs(t - x) / 100.0
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)[single]
    v = d.var()
    if v <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((d - d.mean()) * (r - r.mean())).mean() / v)

results.name: fine_numeric_proximity_gap
results.description: Among targets matching no example's final digit, yes-rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets more than 20 away; observed > null means the model under-produces fine-grained numeric-proximity generalisation (beyond its decade-band term).
results.code:
# name: fine_numeric_proximity_gap
# description: Among targets matching no example's final digit, yes-rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets more than 20 away; observed > null means the model under-produces fine-grained numeric-proximity generalisation (beyond its decade-band term).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = sets.unique()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    mind = np.full(len(df), 1000.0)
    match = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    codes, cats = pd.factorize(sets)
    for i, s in enumerate(cats):
        xs = np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        m = codes == i
        tt = t[m]
        mind[m] = np.abs(tt[:, None] - xs[None, :]).min(axis=1)
        match[m] = np.isin(tt % 10, xs % 10)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    near = (~match) & (mind <= 5) & (mind > 0)
    far = (~match) & (mind > 20)
    if near.sum() == 0 or far.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near].mean() - r[far].mean())

results.name: powers_of_two_concept
results.description: In sets whose examples are all powers of two (2..64), yes-rate on power-of-two targets minus yes-rate on other targets; observed > null means the model under-produces generalisation to the 'powers of two' mathematical concept.
results.code:
# name: powers_of_two_concept
# description: In sets whose examples are all powers of two (2..64), yes-rate on power-of-two targets minus yes-rate on other targets; observed > null means the model under-produces generalisation to the 'powers of two' mathematical concept.
def test_statistic(df):
    P = {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, cats = pd.factorize(sets)
    ok = np.array([all(int(x) in P for x in s.split(",")) and ("," in s) for s in cats])
    inset = ok[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    tp = np.isin(t, list(P))
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = inset & tp
    b = inset & ~tp
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: perfect_square_concept
results.description: In sets with at least two examples that are all perfect squares, yes-rate on perfect-square targets minus non-square targets; observed > null means the model under-produces generalisation to the 'square numbers' concept.
results.code:
# name: perfect_square_concept
# description: In sets with at least two examples that are all perfect squares, yes-rate on perfect-square targets minus non-square targets; observed > null means the model under-produces generalisation to the 'square numbers' concept.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = {k * k for k in range(1, 11)}
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, cats = pd.factorize(sets)
    ok = np.array([("," in s) and all(int(x) in S for x in s.split(",")) for s in cats])
    inset = ok[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    ts = np.isin(t, list(S))
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = inset & ts
    b = inset & ~ts
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
